policy.unit_of_observation: One row represents one metric from one benchmark split and one named system configuration. Never combine metrics from different configurations into a synthetic system.
policy.comparison_ceiling: All included external scores are contextual or historical references unless a separately preregistered matched comparison is recorded; no direct CEB superiority claim is supported by this registry.
policy.uncertainty_rule: Preserve source-reported uncertainty notation. Do not infer a confidence level or interval method unless the source states it.
policy.denominator_rule: Every task or pair count belongs to its exact benchmark/split. Missing denominators must be explicitly marked not_reported, not silently imputed. Candidate-dependent augmented-recall denominators are per-agent discovery diagnostics and must not be used as a common cross-agent ranking denominator.
policy.unlabeled_rule: An unlabeled leaderboard value remains unlabeled; it cannot be mapped to a named metric by guesswork.

comparators.split: Live leaderboard; top listed GLM-5.3 + Claude Code row

sample_denominator.unit: repository release-range sequences; denominator not stated in visible leaderboard row

caveats: The benchmark uses continuous release-history milestone DAGs; it is not a CEB evidence-disposition task set.
The visible leaderboard row does not expose the task denominator, exact aggregation details, uncertainty interval or all run configuration fields.
No metric correspondence here licenses a direct CEB superiority comparison.
Dataset contains 219 PRs from 187 public repositories across 19 languages; exact high-severity TP denominator is not separately stated on the live leaderboard.
Leader row OhMyBug run dated 2026-10-25: 83.0 grounded F1 / 92.0 precision / 75.6 recall.
Grounded scores count findings reviewed by people; these are not all-severity results or CEB Recall@5/actionable-precision scores.
Augmented recall is candidate-dependent because unmatched true positives increase that candidate's numerator and denominator; use grounded recall for common-gold ranking.
The methodology uses a Claude Sonnet 5 classifier for labels and unmatched-finding classification; senior-engineer audit scope is separately disclosed.
Nine C/C++/Rust systems projects, including Firefox, V8 and OpenSSL.
217 cases pass mechanical checks and 48 use human adjudication; each has a fixed companion.
Measures target-mechanism recall across findings, not top-five recall or ordinary-PR vulnerability prevalence.
68% of analyzed misses locate a root-cause file but explain a neighboring/incorrect mechanism.
Fixed companions check the target only and do not establish report precision; fixed revisions can include intervening changes.
The evaluator is Claude Opus 5.5, also an evaluated model; one run per task and unmatched budgets limit comparisons.
174 verified instances derived from a 584-instance corpus; 11 Python repositories, with Django contributing 63 tasks.
Each instance has one labeled known defect; other true defects are not necessarily counted as KDDR hits.
KDDR and Usefulness Rate are separate; useful comments are not necessarily target-defect detections.
Table 7 ± values are sample SD across three judges, not sampling confidence intervals; Table 8 reports per-judge bootstrap intervals.
The reference/judge lineage and 60-comment human study are limited; agents in the study did not use tools or execute code.
Five repositories: cal.com, Discourse, Grafana, Keycloak and Sentry; languages Go, Java, Python, Ruby and TypeScript.
13 model configurations; Kodus harness, API access path, replay execution and Claude Haiku 4.5 judge.
DeepSeek V4 Pro is the current top row: F1 43.9, precision 43.6%, recall 44.2%, 42/95 gold bugs found, estimated $0.30/PR and $0.21/bug found.
The 95% bootstrap interval 32.3–56.3 is for recall, based on 2,000 resamples over 30 PRs; not a CI for F1 or model run-to-run variance.
The three independent re-scores assess judge noise on the same findings; each model entry had one agent pass, so model run-to-run variance is unmeasured.

Ground truth is bugs human reviewers had already flagged before merge. Bugs that escaped the original human review are outside the labeled denominator, so the benchmark measures recovery of known human-found bugs rather than exhaustive defect discovery.
Leaderboard coverage varies by model; inspect each scorecard's evaluated golden denominator before cross-model comparison.
Maintained by Kodus, which also supplies the harness; treat as vendor-maintained contextual evidence, not independent multi-harness replication.

sample_denominator.unit: per-tool PR denominators differ; dashboard reports a pooled 17,768 scored-PR view for the recent period

caveats: Analyzes production review-bot activity, developer responses, follow-up code changes and resolved threads; uses LLM-powered analysis of suggestion adoption.
Dashboard states 17,768 scored PRs in its recent-period view, while individual tool sample sizes vary; not a shared paired denominator.
The visible all-time PR totals and recent-period sample sizes are different quantities; do not combine them.
Adoption or a resulting code change is not independent proof that a review finding is factually correct or causally valid.
No CEB causal mechanism labels, exact P/I/F/N/M/IRR controls, top-five recall equivalence or human minutes are reported.
Open-world repository-level multi-bug discovery and repair; agents receive no issue descriptions or bug locations.

October 1 paper's strongest evaluated system reports 4.7%; the live leaderboard viewed 2026-11-07 lists Astra 6 / mini-SWE-agent at 9.5%; these are different snapshots/configurations and must not be spliced.
The denominator is 4,068 bugs across 100 repositories and 22 languages, not issue-conditioned tasks.
Each repaired bug is checked by its own hidden fail-to-pass tests, and the original suite checks for regressions; the benchmark's population still derives from upstream issue/PR histories.
Not equivalent to CEB's issue-specific task resolve_rate; no direct superiority claim is licensed.
Reference result is GPT-5-mini 46/70 = 65.7%, one attempt per task, no escalation or repair loop.
The pool later grew to 89 tasks, but the published 46/70 reference remains on the original 70-task denominator.
Narrow population: reproducible, maintainer-tested Python library fixes in the pinned Python 3.13 container, not the general software-bug population.
The deterministic gate checks a named fail-to-pass test; this does not establish whole-repository correctness, causal uniqueness or CEB independent pristine regrade.
The default runner is sandboxed, but the optional agentic path is not; respect the project's host-execution warning.

comparators.benchmark_name: Kodus State of AI Code Review 2026
caveats: Across 22,743 AI-authored PRs in the report's supported GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket/Azure DevOps pipeline; data window begins 2025-09-01 and snapshot ends 2026-06-08.
33% of 180,739 review suggestions were classified implemented/adapted by changes to flagged lines in later diffs.
A later diff is not proof the specific suggestion caused the change or that the resulting change was correct.
The rate by PR-created month rises from 25% to 48% over the cited eight-month period; recent months are right-censored and June is partial.
Descriptive platform analytics, not randomized treatment effects or independent human truth adjudication.

comparators.benchmark_name: Kodus State of AI Code Review 2026
caveats: 34.5% of bug-class suggestions were classified implemented/adapted by later changes to flagged lines.
This is an uptake/implementation outcome, not defect precision, correctness or verified remediation.
Later changes can be independently motivated, bundled or unrelated; the source's rule detects changes to flagged lines rather than causal attribution.
Descriptive data from the Kodus production pipeline, not a randomized treatment effect.

comparators.benchmark_name: Kodus State of AI Code Review 2026
caveats: 31.2% of security-class suggestions were classified implemented/adapted by later changes to flagged lines.
This is not vulnerability correctness, verified security remediation or incident reduction.
The report's implementation classifier and open-flag measures include false positives and accepted risk; no claim of causal attribution is made.

comparators.benchmark_name: Kodus State of AI Code Review 2026
comparators.split: Flagged merged PRs; at least one flag remains open
caveats: 71.8% of 13,609 flagged merged PRs had at least one flag still open.
The open flag includes false positives and accepted risk; this is not a defect escape rate or a rate of unremediated true bugs.
Do not mix this PR-level denominator with the suggestion-level denominator of 180,739.
41 tasks run on one H100 and 12 on CPU; the hardware mix is part of the benchmark contract.
11 models / 31 effort configurations; fixed mini-SWE-agent harness; three complete runs per configuration.
Highest displayed mean Pass@1 is 75% for Claude Opus 5 max and GPT-5.6 Sol max; cost/time trade-offs differ significantly.
The benchmark verifier checks functionality and selected regressions; it explicitly does not claim to assess merge readiness or general code quality.
This is production inference engineering on SGLang, not a matched CEB repair task population.

comparators.split: 19 tasks with E2E serving coverage; full verifier versus E2E checks excluded
caveats: Same patches on the 19 E2E-covered tasks: 69.4% pass when E2E checks are excluded versus 45.9% with the full verifier.
Pooled verifier-scope ablation, not a model-specific leaderboard row.
This is a verification-boundary effect for the selected serving tasks, not a universal expected E2E penalty.
489 tasks paired between isolated phase evaluation and FullCycle from a bare repository.
FullCycle integrates environment reconstruction, implementation and verification-test generation; no human scaffolding is provided.
No model exceeds 14% strict FullCycle solve in the reported table; GLM-5.1 is highest at 13.50%.
SWE-Judge combines static and dynamic evaluation; FullCycle judge-human alignment is 96.9% on 489 annotated instances.
Model list, harness, judge and task population differ from CEB; not a direct CEB pass-rate comparator.
13 models; four independent runs; fresh empty workspace, installation script and fresh-container hidden tests.
Claude Opus 5 xhigh reaches 67.7% Pass@1, the highest table result; Fable 5 high reports 65.3%; GPT-5.6 Sol max 61.2%.
This is greenfield whole-repository generation from implementation-independent specifications, not maintenance of an existing repository or PR review.
The authors perform static specification/test alignment and rollout-guided task auditing; 59.4% of a separate 138-task SWE-Bench Verified audit is not a result on E2E-SWE.

comparators.benchmark_version: Journal of Systems and Software, 2026, DOI 10.1016/j.jss.2026.112931
comparators.split: Runtime root-cause analysis across PetShop, RE1 and RE3

sample_denominator.unit: benchmark_instances; exact task denominator not recorded here

caveats: Runtime root-cause localization over monitored signals, not source-only pre-merge PR review.
Uses causal graphs, in-distribution counterfactual interventions and Shapley-style contribution allocation; contribution allocation alone is not causal identification.
Reports Recall@1/Recall@3 in its own runtime RCA setting; these are not CEB Recall@5 or ReviewBench grounded F1.
Task denominator, exact system configurations and uncertainty must be taken from the paper before any quantitative replication.
Uses execution profiles combining predicate outcomes and variable values for causal statistical fault localization.
The published 835 program-version population is a fault-localization dataset denominator, not PR review tasks.
Execution-profile evidence is not equivalent to source-only counterfactual predictions or human-adjudicated review comments.
Do not compare its fault-localization rank directly with CEB defect Recall@5.
